title: What is our semantic layer? (definition & boundary)
whyItMatters: Every later decision (home, governance, tooling) inherits its scope from this sentence. An unbounded definition produces an unbuildable layer.
question: One paragraph that says what the semantic layer is — and an explicit boundary list of what it is not. Open point: are metrics and dimensions (calculations, not just concepts) in scope?
recommendation: The enterprise semantic layer is the Semantic Control Plane: namespaces, certified concepts with stable URIs, mapping records, and federation edges. Metric and dimension calculation logic stays beside the layer; KPI names may mapsTo a Concept.
isIn: Concept names for metrics as meaning targets
Policies gating binds to approved concepts
isOut: Collibra Guided Stewardship Data Model / Entity / Attribute
Physical tables, columns, files (Technical Catalog)
Data product identity and ODCS lifecycle (Marketplace)
Glossary prose and steward UI (Collibra)
SQL / DAX / MDX / semantic-model measure formulas
BI tool models as a second meaning SoR
evidence: WS5 — metrics in or beside the layer
deliverable: One-page definition with is/is-not boundary (written last at W6).

detailSections.heading: Definition
paragraphs: The enterprise semantic layer is the shared system of canonical meaning: scoped namespaces, certified concepts with stable URIs, mapping records that bind catalog and product artifacts to those concepts, and federation edges that align NATCO or import meanings to the global core.
It answers “what does this word mean for the enterprise?” — not “where is the table?” and not “how is the KPI calculated?”

detailSections.heading: Metrics boundary (WS5)
paragraphs: POC recommendation: calculations stay beside the layer. A KPI name may live in the Business Catalog and mapsTo a Concept (kind metric if needed). Formula, grain, and tool-specific measures live in BI or a metrics store.
If leadership puts calculations inside the layer at W6, scope and tooling cost expand materially.

residual: WS5 confirms BI metrics stay beside the layer at W6.

title: Where does the registry live? (system of record)
whyItMatters: The authority matrix requires exactly one system of record per metadata kind; the semantic row was the open one.
question: Marketplace (Entropy) or Git — which system is SoR for concepts, ontologies and mappings? Separated from SQ3: record and interaction surface may differ.
recommendation: Git Contracts (Semantic Control Plane pack) is SoR for concepts, ontologies, mappings, and federation. Entropy Marketplace is SoR for products; Collibra for glossary prose. Marketplace may render meaning; it does not own it. Neo4j is a query materialisation, not SoR.
isOut: Entropy as sole writable meaning SoR
Neo4j as authoritative store
Collibra as enterprise concept SoR
deliverable: Decision paper with frozen criteria: authoring friction, review/approval, versioning fidelity, API access, Ossie I/O, operational cost.

detailSections.heading: Authority split
bullets: Concepts / namespaces / mappings / federation → Git SCP

detailSections.heading: Asymmetry corrected
paragraphs: WS1 builds ontology depth on the marketplace path. This POC exercises the Git path with equal depth (Contracts packs + Neo4j seed + enrich). Git is the candidate SoR; marketplace is the candidate experience surface (SQ3).

detailSections.heading: Vendor demo must prove
bullets: Entropy can render concepts without becoming the only writable copy
Round-trip to Ossie/Git without losing URI, lifecycle, mapping ids
Approval hooks that map to steward SLA

residual: Vendor workshop validates Entropy as render/edit UI with Git still SoR.

title: How do people and machines interact? (experience)
whyItMatters: Federation lives or dies on domain self-service; a registry only architects can use is a bottleneck with a wiki attached.
question: Authoring (domain adds concept), review (steward approves), browsing (consumer navigates concept → product), and machine interface (API for contracts, Model AI, agents).
recommendation: Four journeys demable in this Grid: Contracts folders (producer), governance + MappingRecord (steward), Marketplace → Semantics (consumer), /api/kg/* (machine). SoR (SQ2) and UX may differ.
isOut: Architects doing all domain authoring
Moving SoR silently during UX co-design
deliverable: Co-designed experience blueprint (producer, steward, consumer, machine) with vendor.

detailSections.heading: Producer
paragraphs: Domain member proposes a concept via PR to the SCP pack or Contracts UI, with URI, namespace, kind, and optional draft mapping.

detailSections.heading: Steward
paragraphs: Review → approve to lifecycle approved (POL-SEM-02). Reject or escalate conflicts per SQ4.

detailSections.heading: Consumer
paragraphs: Discover in Marketplace, open Semantics Q3 lineage for a product, trust only approved concept binds.

detailSections.heading: Machine
paragraphs: GET /api/kg/health and queries; POST run for Q1–Q7 / N1–N5; ODCS authoritativeDefinitions resolve to concept IRIs.

residual: 24 Aug co-design polish with vendor; must not change SoR.

title: What is our governance model — including conflict?
whyItMatters: Governance that has never processed a disagreement is a diagram. The first real conflict will otherwise be settled by seniority, not process.
question: Charter flows (domain PR, architecture promotions, product field maps) must be exercised by domain people. Unstated half: dispute resolution when two domains claim the same term incompatibly.
recommendation: Happy path: draft → review → approved. Conflict path: freeze global claims → convene → federate, disambiguate, or defer → decision_ref → notify. PoC provoke: Customer vs NATCO local terms resolved by federation.
isOut: Architects performing all adds
Meeting-only decisions with no decision_ref
deliverable: Governance handbook v1 validated by: N domain PRs · one promotion E2E · one conflict through the mechanism.

detailSections.heading: Conflict resolution steps
bullets: Freeze — neither claim approved in global until resolved
Decide — federate, disambiguate URIs, or defer NatCo-only
Notify — product and mapping owners if binds change

detailSections.heading: PoC provoke case
paragraphs: Kunde / Kupac / Ügyfél / Klient vs Customer: incompatible local labels, compatible meaning via federation to global/Customer — resolved by process, not seniority.

residual: Domain PR counts and walked conflict event from WS1/WS2.

title: How do concepts, ontologies and mappings version?
whyItMatters: Without a lifecycle, “deprecated” means “someone said so in a meeting”; without mapping versioning, semantic quality claims are unverifiable.
question: Three artifacts version differently: concept lifecycle states, ontology semver, and mapping versions that can break while concepts stay stable.
recommendation: Concepts: draft → review → approved/active → deprecated → retired. Ontologies: semver on namespace slices. Mappings: first-class MappingRecord versions; most real-world drift lives here.
isIn: Concept lifecycle states and breaking-change rules
isOut: Treating concept stability as proof that mappings are correct
evidence: WS6 TM Forum deprecation and remapping
deliverable: One lifecycle & versioning specification covering all three artifacts.

detailSections.heading: Ontology semver
paragraphs: MAJOR: removed/merged concepts — consumers must remap. MINOR: additive. PATCH: editorial.

detailSections.heading: Mapping versioning
paragraphs: A concept can be stable while its mapping is wrong. Quality claims cite mapping version + concept version together.

residual: WS6 supplies TM Forum deprecation cases.

title: What is the canonisation strategy? (promotion and demotion)
whyItMatters: “Thin global core” is a design principle; without demotion the core only grows into the canonical vocabulary the charter forbids.
question: Criteria for a domain concept entering the global core, and the reverse path when usage does not materialise.
recommendation: Promote when ≥2 domains/NatCos (or enterprise product spanning NatCos), stable window (POC default 30 days), no unresolved conflict, recorded approval, and at least one consumer. Demote when usage fails to materialise.
isIn: Customer federation as PoC promotion evidence
isOut: Promotion by exception with no demotion path
Core growth without usage evidence
evidence: Charter success criterion 3 — one promotion E2E
deliverable: Canonisation criteria in the governance handbook + one executed promotion.

detailSections.heading: Promotion criteria (all required)
bullets: Used by ≥2 domains or NatCos (or multi-NatCo product family)
At least one product or mapping ready to bind

detailSections.heading: Demotion triggers
bullets: Never federated after exception → retire or move off global

residual: Formal walked promotion event recorded at W6.

title: Who consumes the layer, and what can they do that they could not before?
whyItMatters: Feasibility without a consumer convinces nobody. Producer work is cost; consumers are the return.
question: Name consumers and demonstrate: marketplace concept→products; BI definition pickup; external platform consume; one agent-shaped query.
recommendation: Three live journeys plus one machine-driven query. POC stand-ins: Marketplace→Q3, Concept definition for BI pattern, kg-api for platforms, Q6/Q3 for agent-shaped “which products implement Customer?”
isOut: Slide-only consumer stories without live demo
deliverable: Three named consumer journeys demonstrated live; one machine-driven.

detailSections.heading: Journeys
bullets: (a) Marketplace user: product → Semantics lineage to SID Concept
(b) BI: pull concept definition/URI; measures stay beside (SQ1)
(c) External platform: kg-api / package import (WS4 harness)
(d) Agent: curated Cypher/API answering product↔concept questions

residual: WS4/WS5 live demos at W6; replace Customer stand-in with churn/network when data exists.

title: How does meaning bind to data, and what does it cost?
whyItMatters: Binding is more load-bearing than the ontology. Leadership will ask cost per product — need a number, not an adjective.
question: Field→concept convention is ratified (ODCS authoritativeDefinitions). Open: who maps, with what assist, cost per contract, and schema-break behaviour.
recommendation: Playbook: inventory → AI first pass → steward confirm → MappingRecord + ODCS refs → drift on change. Measure greenfield vs retrofit hours.
isOut: Unmeasured “AI will make it cheap” claims
deliverable: Mapping playbook + measured effort per contract (greenfield vs retrofit).

detailSections.heading: Cost template
paragraphs: Fill median hours: greenfield + AI (Chris), retrofit + AI (Mihai), manual baseline. Report automated vs manual share from WS1.

residual: Measured hours from Mihai and Chris by W5.

title: How do we detect semantic drift?
whyItMatters: A registry that only accretes becomes confidently wrong. Drift detection keeps “trust as data” honest.
question: Governance covers who may change meaning; nothing yet detects silent divergence — e.g. schema change breaks mappings.
recommendation: Stub: scheduled AI remapping pass, diff vs MappingRecord set, steward triage. Cadence weekly for pilot. Automate tickets in autumn.
isOut: Assuming approved mappings stay correct forever
deliverable: Drift-detection concept note + one executed diff demonstration.

detailSections.heading: Mechanism
bullets: Actor — domain steward triage; Architecture owns false-positive rate

title: Who stewards this, with how much time?
whyItMatters: The flywheel dies on steward SLA, not architecture. Also the honest cost line for scaling to all NatCos.
question: Who the stewards are, role vs job, weekly time, and sustainable approval SLA.
recommendation: Named roles with reserved time; pilot SLAs (e.g. 3-day response); measure hours/week in WS1/WS2 before “ontology v1 for all NatCos”.
isIn: Domain / global steward / product owner / Architecture roles
isOut: Unnamed “someone will steward” assumptions
evidence: Measured steward effort in WS1 and WS2 during PoC
deliverable: Stewardship operating note: roles, measured effort, SLA, funding per domain/NatCo.

detailSections.heading: Proposed pilot SLAs
bullets: Concept draft → first response: 3 business days

residual: Fill hours/week from real people in WS1/WS2.

title: Does the Apache Ossie bet hold? (portability proof)
whyItMatters: Buy-no-tool-now rests on portability. One successful round-trip retires risk; one failure changes strategy.
question: Round-trip one domain ontology: export Ossie form → import second tool → verify nothing load-bearing is lost.
recommendation: Ossie is interchange, not a second SoR. Protocol: export Customer slice → Palantir (WS4) → checklist URIs, lifecycle, mappings, federation → verdict Hold / Hold with gaps / Fail.
isOut: “Aligned with Ossie” as slogan without a test
deliverable: Round-trip report: exported, survived, lost, verdict.

detailSections.heading: Acceptable loss
paragraphs: Tool UI layout, display hints, Neo4j internal ids.

residual: Execute harness with Thorsten; vendor notes from workshop.

title: What changes in the metadata strategy?
decisionGate: Draft W6 · ratify with strategy owners
whyItMatters: The PoC is not an island — outcomes must amend strategy docs leadership already knows, or they evaporate.
question: Which authority-matrix rows change, what Phase 1+ inherits, and which semantic rules become compliance bar v2 candidates (score-only first).
recommendation: Close semantic SoR row with Git SCP (SQ2). Transition: pilot Customer + NatCos, Marketplace product SoR, Collibra glossary, drift stub→job, Ossie before tool sprawl. Score-only SEM-V2 rules before enforce.
isOut: Leaving strategy docs unchanged after W6
deliverable: Amendment PR to metadata-management-strategy (+ matrix, + transition) and v2 rule-candidate list for dp-compliance-rules.

detailSections.heading: Compliance candidates (score-only)
bullets: SEM-V2-01 — binds only to approved concepts
SEM-V2-03 — MappingRecord present for each crosswalk
SEM-V2-04 — deprecated has replaced_by in notify window
SEM-V2-05 — NatCo concepts federate when used in enterprise products

residual: Vincent + strategy owners ratify external strategy doc path.
